A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections 7–10 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original optical-flow and intensity-reconstruction evaluations, qualitative results, and ablations in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a single-network versus dual-network experiment in Section 4.5 and Table 6.

M1.justification: The proposed U-Net, inputs and outputs, PhE/CMax/regularization losses, training procedure, and inference processing are unchanged. The newly evaluated dual-network variant is a comparator, not a replacement for the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use DSEC, ECD, HDR, and BS-ERGB for the same tasks and scenarios. Describing DSEC driving as 'highway' instead of 'wild' does not accompany any change in evaluated data.

E2.justification: Section 4.5 and Table 6 add a comparator comprising two U-Nets, separately predicting flow and intensity. All existing benchmark comparators remain.

E3.justification: The new experiment compares one versus two U-Nets while explicitly holding the loss function, loss weights, and training settings fixed. Existing splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, and appendix sequence selections remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an architectural comparison testing whether a single shared network outperforms separate flow and intensity networks. The existing loss-removal, flow-only, loss-weight, and contrast-threshold ablations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiment follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds dual-network results: EPE 3.30, AE 10.15, %Out 22.85, MSE 0.11, SSIM 0.29, and LPIPS 0.59. All existing numerical results remain unchanged; this is additional comparison evidence, not improved performance of the proposed model between versions.

T1.justification: The event-generation model, warping equations, PhE derivation, and loss definitions are unchanged. Explicitly stating that constant velocities can differ between pixels clarifies the existing spatially varying flow formulation rather than introducing a new assumption.

C1.justification: The conclusion softens 'shortest inference time among all optical flow approaches' to 'very short inference time' while predicting both quantities, although the stronger claim remains in the abstract. The novelty, accuracy, and generalization claims otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 interprets the new comparison as supporting shared learning of motion, appearance, and their synergies within one network. Section 5 adds joint motion/noise estimation as an alternative to preprocessing outliers. Existing failure conditions and metric limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future source-code release, whereas v2 describes source code as provided. v2 also specifies the dual comparator's two U-Nets and matched training configuration. Existing implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and sequence-cropping disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shiba et al.'s 'Simultaneous motion and noise estimation with event cameras' to the limitations discussion and modestly refines descriptions of existing work. Citation renumbering and publication-metadata updates otherwise preserve the research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory motivation are tightened, terminology and phrasing receive local edits, and Section 4.5 is added. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 6 gains a comparator row and corrected best-value emphasis. Figure labels and spacing are adjusted, and supplementary Figures 6–8 are integrated more compactly with their discussion. The existing visual examples and table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The controlled dual-network comparison strengthens the justification for a single shared architecture beyond v1's loss and flow-only ablations. Clearer prose, corrected table emphasis, and tighter appendix layout also help readers. These are useful but bounded gains: the proposed method and existing benchmark results remain unchanged, and uncertainty reporting is not expanded.
